lead: A circular neighbourhood around a hill, with a park, a viewpoint and plenty of community spirit.
text: The neighbourhood follows the terrain and wraps around the Turó de la Peira, a hill that belonged to the Can Peguera estate and whose park opened in 1936, with about eight hectares of scrub and pine woods and a viewpoint topped by a large iron cross. In the early 1960s, housing construction reduced its extent.

The blocks, with plain, symmetrical windows, sometimes curve around the hill. It is one of the neighbourhoods most affected by aluminosis (a structural decay of concrete): after a building collapsed in 1990, the remodelling of the affected blocks was pushed forward, and its residents have played an active part in it. With 49,090 inhabitants/km², it is one of the densest neighbourhoods in Barcelona.
housing: Blocks of flats from the 1950s and 1960s, many of them remodelled because of aluminosis.
places: Parc del Turó de la Peira
